prompt:
Precise-object-edit. This is ONLY a transparent animation layer of Max's HAND AND FOREARM from Sam & Max Hit the Road. Correct the second reference painting B02 by extracting/repainting ONLY the pale cream hand making a finger-gun gesture: extremely long straight index finger points horizontally to screen-left; thumb sticks vertically up near the right base of that finger; three curled finger creases below it; thick forearm continues downward off the canvas. Source reference 1 shows the exact gesture placement and proportions. Reference 2 shows our paint/color/line style, but ITS WHITE ZIGZAG TEETH ARE A MISTAKE FOR THIS HAND EXTRACTION. DELETE THE ENTIRE MOUTH, ALL TEETH, ALL LIPS, ALL NOSE, FACE, HEAD, TORSO AND MAROON SHADOW. Output only ONE isolated pale cream cartoon hand plus forearm with clean dark thin ink and taupe shading, transparent elsewhere. The long horizontal pointing finger must have smooth rounded straight edges and no zigzags or tooth-shaped pieces. Keep the long left index finger and raised upright thumb distinct. Do not turn it into a simple thumbs-up or index finger pointing upward. Keep the same thumb/forearm placement as reference 2. The hand occupies the left and middle of the original source tile. No borders, no rectangle, no cast-shadow background, no extra fingers, no props. This isolated hand is composited over the existing unmodified Max portrait, so do NOT include even a sliver of grin or face. High-resolution true RGBA alpha.

The full protected job brief is retained below for provenance; THIS call generates only the hand from costume341_1927, not its other layers:
Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Max, the white rabbit-like creature (long ears, wide toothy grin, no clothes), here in close-up in the warm colors of this scene. Keep the colors of the input. The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (1 frame); animation 7 (a separate part the game draws on top of the body, such as the head), facing right (2 frames); animation 8, facing right (2 frames); animation 9, facing right (1 frame). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 68 to 256 pixels tall and from 260 to 448 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig341_02/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.
